expected_sources.role: PAD: datasheet conditions and covenants, components, PBCs, implementation arrangements
Signed Loan Agreement for Loan 9560-JO and TF0C1892

text: Documents: PAD5170 (2023-05-24) and the Loan Agreement for Loan 9560-JO and Trust Fund TF0C1892 (2023-07-16). Jordan borrows from IBRD, so the signed financing document is a Loan Agreement. They match closely; the differences are:

Project description: same objective, 'to improve the efficiency of water services in Jordan' (PAD p. 21; LA Schedule 1, p. 6). The LA describes the same five parts but names Part 4 'Institutional strengthening for water sector efficiency' with 4.1 project management and 4.2 PBC verification and audit support, where the PAD datasheet calls Component 4 'Project management and implementation support' (PAD p. 7; LA p. 8). The PAD gives costs by component (US$209m, 54m, 27m, 10m, 0) and the PBC amounts (e.g. PBC 2 US$21.4 million) (PAD pp. 7, 24); the LA instead allocates the loan by category and implementer: WAJ (Parts 1, 2, 4), MoWI (Part 3.1), JVA (Part 3.2), Eligible PBC Expenditures, CERC, front-end fee, split into non-concessional and concessional (GCFF) portions totalling US$200 million and US$50 million (LA pp. 16-17).

Effectiveness conditions: (a) the WAJ Subsidiary Agreement executed with its conditions met - same in both. (b) differs in wording: the PAD datasheet lists a 'JVA Cooperation Agreement' (PAD p. 10), the LA a 'JVA Subsidiary Agreement' (LA Section 5.01(b), p. 4; Schedule 2 Section I.B, p. 10). The LA adds a 120-day effectiveness deadline (5.02) and a four-month deadline for the co-financing agreement's effectiveness (4.01) (LA p. 4); the PAD lists the latter as a covenant (PAD p. 9).

Disbursement conditions: the PAD datasheet lists none. The LA sets them (Schedule 2, Section III.B, p. 18): withdrawals pari passu between the non-concessional and concessional portions (79.96/20.04 until the co-financing agreement is signed, then 66.61/16.69); retroactive financing up to US$799,599 plus US$200,401 for payments from 1 January 2023; PBC withdrawals only with evidence verified by the Audit Bureau (payments made per the POM) and by the Verification Agent (PBC achieved); CERC withdrawals only after an eligible emergency is accepted.

Implementing arrangements: consistent. Both have MOPIC and MWI with overall responsibility, the WAJ-PMU for day-to-day implementation with additional staff within six months, an Oversight and Coordination Committee chaired by MOPIC and a Steering Committee chaired by MWI, both within three months of effectiveness, and a Project Operations Manual (PAD pp. 9-10, 34-35; LA pp. 9-10). The PAD covenant asks for the POM within four months and an independent verification agency within six months (PAD p. 10); the LA adds the WAJ and JVA subsidiary agreements and WC cooperation agreements for the water companies (LA p. 10) and semester project reports within one month (LA p. 16).
Later change, outside this comparison: the March 2026 restructuring amends the agreement (PBCs, eligible expenditures, MWI's category moved to WAJ, Audit Bureau as PBC verifier).
